name: Discrete Fibromuscular Subaortic Stenosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Discrete Subaortic Stenosis

criteria.description: Presence of a discrete fibromuscular membrane or ridge in the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) detected by echocardiography
Demonstration of a significant pressure gradient (>30 mmHg) across the LVOT on Doppler echocardiography
Exclusion of other causes of LVOT obstruction such as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or valvular aortic stenosis
Presence of characteristic clinical features such as systolic murmur and exertional dyspnea

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a discrete fibromuscular membrane in the LVOT with a significant pressure gradient on echocardiography and exclusion of other LVOT obstruction causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiographic findings supported by clinical presentation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Systolic ejection murmur at the left lower sternal border
searchTerms: heart sound at left lower sternum

pathognomonic.symptomName: Discrete fibromuscular subaortic membrane visualized on echocardiography
searchTerms: fibrous membrane below aortic valve on echo
subaortic membrane seen in heart ultrasound

rare.symptomName: Aortic regurgitation secondary to membrane extension
searchTerms: leaky aortic valve from membrane growth
aortic valve leakage due to obstruction

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific laboratory biomarkers
imaging: Echocardiography showing discrete fibromuscular membrane in LVOT
Doppler echocardiography demonstrating elevated LVOT pressure gradient
Cardiac MRI may delineate membrane and assess ventricular function
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be sporadic or familial in rare cases
other: Electrocardiogram may show left ventricular hypertrophy or strain pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Asymmetric septal hypertrophy without discrete membrane
Dynamic LVOT obstruction with systolic anterior motion of mitral valve
Family history and genetic testing may support diagnosis
Calcific or congenital aortic valve abnormalities
Valve leaflet thickening and restricted motion on echocardiography

redFlags: Progressive increase in LVOT pressure gradient
references: Gersony WM. Discrete subaortic stenosis. Circulation. 1993;87(3):800-805.
Maron BJ, et al. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and discrete subaortic stenosis: differential diagnosis and management. J Am Coll Cardiol. 1995;26(3): 738-742.
